thread:
Kai (sre-oncall): seeing sustained increase in streaming worker queue depth and p99 response time since 14:02 UTC. Latency climbs once we hit 240k active streams. Backend GPU hosts show high mem pressure. I'm going to propose a short dampening action: mute streaming responses for web clients and force buffered fallback for 10m while autoscaling and cache warmups complete.

Maria (infra): agree. we've got KV cache misses spiking and many prefix replays. If we don't act we'll risk broader request failures.

Paul (platform): thumbs up to a quick switch. Suggest we implement a soft circuit-breaker first (reject new streaming sessions with a clear 503 + Retry-After) rather than killing existing completions mid-flight. That will let clients degrade gracefully.

Jen (support): what's the customer-visible impact? do we need a status page entry and customer emails?

incident-bot: "INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-045 - Streaming throughput degradation. Priority: P1. Pageres: @sre-oncall."

Kai (sre-oncall): yes, short visible degradation: streaming responses (server-sent events / chunked SSE) will be temporarily disabled. Clients will get non-streaming buffered responses or 503 indicating fallback. Expected window: 10-20 minutes while we expand capacity and warm caches. Please draft status note.

Maria (infra): I'll flip the traffic-shaper to limit new streaming handshakes and enable buffering. Rolling change to feature-flag service now.

Paul (platform): sending the toggle via internal feature API: 
```
curl -X POST "https://internal-control.redwood/api/v1/feature-toggle"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"feature":"streaming_responses","state":"disabled","scope":"global","reason":"throttle-to-stabilize-2026-03-15"}'
```

deploy-bot: Feature toggle request accepted. Change id: FT-8624. Applied to routing control plane.

Maria (infra): applied routing change on canary (10% traffic) at 14:09 UTC. Observing reduced connection churn. Increasing to 50% now.

Kai (sre-oncall): switching pager to Maria for active mitigation window. Handoff: I'm stepping out at 14:12 UTC. Maria, can you own until 14:45 and then hand back? @OpsScheduler please keep an eye for rollback triggers.

OpsScheduler: noted. Will monitor quotas and error budget. Setting alert: streaming_connect_errors > 5% for 5m -> page platform-sd.

Jen (support): draft status update for status.redwood.ai: 
"We are investigating increased latency and connection issues for streaming responses. We are temporarily disabling streaming to stabilize the service. Users will receive buffered responses or retryable errors; no data loss expected. We will post updates here and via email for affected enterprise customers."

Maria (infra): metrics look better at 50% mute: p99 token latency down from 2.3s -> 1.1s, streaming worker queue depth halved. Proceeding to 100% at 14:16 UTC.

Paul (platform): quick note to client SDK teams: add a clear fallback response in the next client patch to prefer buffered mode when 503/Retry-After encountered. Example: 
```
if (resp.status === 503 && resp.headers['retry-after']) {
  // switch to buffered poll mode
}
```

Kai (sre-oncall): Maria, once you're stable for 5m and error rates are within bounds, we can start a controlled re-enable on a slow ramp (10% -> 25% -> 50% over 15m) with automatic rollback if connection failures exceed threshold.

Maria (infra): agreed. Using the ramp plan and will keep autoscaling knobs open. If memory pressure returns we revert to 0% streaming.

Jen (support): notifying top 10 enterprise customers via email template. Copy below for review: 
"Hello — We're currently experiencing high load affecting real-time streaming features. We've temporarily switched streaming to a buffered fallback while we stabilize performance. This is a temporary mitigation; no data loss is expected. We're monitoring and will send updates. Contact support if you see persistent errors"

Paul (platform): created a quick dashboard link for execs and SRE: https://grafana.redwood/d/streaming-ops?panelId=7

Maria (infra): 14:21 UTC: 100% mute in place. Key metrics: CPU/GPU usage on inference hosts down 28%, connection churn down 63%. No new customer error spike beyond expected retry noise.

incident-bot: "INCIDENT UPDATE: FT-8624 applied. Mitigation in progress. Next update at 14:35 UTC or sooner on major change."

Kai (sre-oncall): Thank you. I'm marking this 'mitigating' and handing off monitoring. Maria, please escalate if you see errors > 2% for 10m. Jen, continue customer comms.

Maria (infra): Will do. Leaving sticky notes for re-enable plan and rollback thresholds in the change runbook.

Jen (support): status page updated and enterprise pings sent. Will consolidate customer responses here.

Paul (platform): after we stabilise, let's follow up with a post-incident action: improve streaming admission control, proactively warm KV prefixes for long-lived sessions, and consider a soft start queue to pace new handshakes.

Maria (infra): 14:36 UTC: metrics steady. Initiating slow re-enable to 10% at 14:37 UTC. Monitoring autoscaler and mem pressure.

Kai (sre-oncall): back oncall (I resumed) — thanks for taking over, Maria. I'll stay on thread until fully re-enabled.

Maria (infra): 14:48 UTC: re-enable to 25% -> all green. Rolling to 50% now. No customer-visible errors above baseline.

Jen (support): customers reporting normal behaviour, some increased poll retries but clear fallbacks working.

incident-bot: "INCIDENT RESOLVED: Streaming degraded behavior mitigated and rolling re-enable in progress. Incident will remain open for postmortem."

Kai (sre-oncall): closing mitigation loop. Postmortem owners: Maria + Paul + Jen. Please file follow-up with timeline and action items (ads: admission control, client SDK guidance, capacity plan).
